paragraphs.lt: “Bread?”
“Bread,” answers Don Andrés, very slowly. “Bread.”
“Bread.” “Thank you.”

On Tuesday, Don Andrés teaches another word: “agua.” On Wednesday, “leche.” On Thursday, Doña Amparo teaches “hola” and “adiós”—“hello” and “goodbye.” Now, in the mornings, the bakery is a small classroom, and the teachers are learning too: the man is Piotr, he’s from Poland and works at the port. His wife and daughter live in Kraków.

timeline.text: Don Andrés and Marta sell bread in a small bakery in Valencia.
Don Andrés y Marta venden pan en una panadería pequeña de Valencia.
At five past seven, every day, a tall man in work clothes comes in.
A las siete y cinco, todos los días, entra un hombre alto con ropa de trabajo.
He buys a loaf of bread, pays, and doesn’t say a word.
Compra un pan, paga y no habla.
The man looks at the bread, looks at the coins, and doesn’t answer.
El hombre mira el pan, mira las monedas y no contesta.
“He’s an unfriendly man,” remarks Doña Amparo, the neighbor on the first floor.
—Es un hombre antipático —comenta doña Amparo, la vecina del primero.
One Monday, the man touches the bread with a finger and asks:
Un lunes, el hombre toca el pan con un dedo y pregunta:
On Tuesday, Don Andrés teaches another word: “agua.”
El martes, don Andrés enseña otra palabra: «agua».
On Thursday, Doña Amparo teaches “hola” and “adiós”—“hello” and “goodbye.”
El jueves, doña Amparo enseña «hola» y «adiós».
Now, in the mornings, the bakery is a small classroom, and the teachers are learning too: the man is Piotr, he’s from Poland and works at the port.
Ahora, por las mañanas, la panadería es una clase pequeña, y los profesores también aprenden: el hombre es Piotr, es de Polonia y trabaja en el puerto.
His wife and daughter live in Kraków.
Su mujer y su hija viven en Cracovia.

Piotr looks on and doesn’t understand.
Marta explains with her hands: first the guy, then the lady, then Doña Amparo… and then you.
Marta explica con las manos: primero el chico, después la señora, después doña Amparo… y después tú.
The next Saturday, a lot of people come in again.
El sábado siguiente entran otra vez muchas personas.
Piotr arrives, looks at everyone, and asks out loud:

At ten past seven, he looks at the door again.
A las siete y diez, mira la puerta otra vez.
At a quarter past seven, Piotr comes in with a woman and a little girl.
A las siete y cuarto, entra Piotr con una mujer y una niña.
The girl looks at the bread and announces, very seriously:

Now Don Andrés also learns a word every morning.
